summary: The Pipeline Safety Authorization Act of 2026 amends federal laws related to pipeline transportation to improve safety standards, update enforcement and hearing procedures, adjust civil penalties, and authorize funding for pipeline safety programs through fiscal year 2031. The bill establishes a voluntary information-sharing system for pipeline safety data, sets new criteria for State excavation damage prevention programs, and modifies special permit rules.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to increased maximum civil penalties for violations, new provisions regarding formal hearings for enforcement actions over $125,000, and opportunities to voluntarily participate in a confidential safety information-sharing system.
Required to adopt specific leading practices for one-call notification and damage prevention programs and data reporting standards to qualify for certain federal grants.
Tasked with establishing new hearing protocols, managing special permit timelines, reviewing waiver terms, and overseeing the voluntary information-sharing system.
affected_groups.group: Federal regulators (Department of Transportation and PHMSA)

key_provisions: Authorizes appropriations of $180,786,000 annually for gas and hazardous liquid programs, $30,000,000 from the Oil Spill Liability Trust Fund, and $7,000,000 for underground natural gas storage safety from fiscal years 2027 through 2031.
Requires the Secretary of Transportation to provide an opportunity for a formal hearing in enforcement matters where compliance costs or proposed civil penalties reach or exceed $125,000.
Establishes a confidential, voluntary pipeline safety information-sharing system (VIS) governed by a 15-member board representing government, industry, and public safety stakeholders.
Increases the maximum civil penalties for pipeline safety violations to $341,200 for a single violation and $3,412,000 for a related series of violations.
Requires States to adopt leading practices for one-call notification programs and excavation damage prevention to remain eligible for certain grants.
Updates minimum safety standards to specify consideration of safety and economic benefits and costs within the United States.
Expands criminal penalties to cover damaging, destroying, or impairing the operation of pipeline facilities under construction.
missing_information: The total overall economic impact on private entities or state budgets is not quantified beyond authorized federal spending levels.
Specific details on the exact operating rules of the third-party data manager for the VIS are left to future administrative rulemaking and board governance.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Pipeline Safety Authorization Act of 2026 amends federal laws related to pipeline transportation to improve safety standards, update enforcement and hearing procedures, adjust civil penalties, and authorize funding for pipeline safety programs through fiscal year 2031. The bill establishes a voluntary information-sharing system for pipeline safety data, sets new criteria for State excavation damage prevention programs, and modifies special permit rules.
summary_detail.significance: The legislation reauthorizes federal pipeline safety programs and funding through 2031 while altering enforcement mechanisms, raising penalties, and creating cooperative data-sharing structures across government, industry, and public safety advocates.
